newsitem.title: USA: St Paul to sell arena and office bonds in late '97.
newsitem.headline: St Paul to sell arena and office bonds in late '97.

text.p: St. Paul officials plan to sell $30 million of bonds for a new downtown arena and $34 million of bonds for a new office development in the fourth quarter of 1997, city Finance Director Joe Reid said Thursday.
The arena financing approved by the City Council in May will be revenue bonds backed with the general obligation of the city, Reid said.
St. Paul plans a $130 million arena for a National Hockey League Expansion franchise scheduled to begin play in fall 2000.
The city has pledged an additional $65 million of bonds if state lawmakers do not include funding in their capital spending bill next year.
St. Paul plans to issue taxable and tax-exempt tax increment financing bonds for the downtown office, retail and parking facility planned to house the Lawson Software Co headquarters, Reid said.
The bonds will be backed with the general obligation of St. Paul and are expected to be sold in late November or early December, Reid said.
About $11 million of the proceeds will be used to acquire and clear property, about $16 million for parking and the remainder for various needs, Reid said.
